text:
anya: ran an nsys + perfetto pass on the 8xA100 job that regressed after the batching heuristic change. attached timeline: https://perfetto.dev/trace/FAKE_TRACE_ID

carl: saw that. quick skim: NVLink transfers + NCCL allreduce are overlapping but kernel launch density drops right after the first couple of tokens. looks like a pipeline bubble.

matt: can you paste the nsys command you used? i want to reproduce locally.

anya: sure — used the usual spicy combo:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,nvtx,nvtx —sample=none --output=regress_8xA100 \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --backtrace all --stats true \
  --force-overwrite --sample-freq=0 --cpuctx-switched
```
then exported to perfetto and filtered for cudaMemcpyAsync / kernel launches / nccl.

zara: fwiw the job config included the batching heuristic tweak: opt_batcher.window_ms = 15 -> 30 and prefer_large_batch = true. that allowed bigger batches but increased tail latency earlier.

carl: i think the heuristic change caused longer groupings of sequences with very uneven lengths, which exposed an inter-GPU imbalance. NCCL allreduce is waiting on the slowest rank and we get KV cache retire churn on fast ranks. you can see rank 3 spending ~15ms idle in the perfetto swimlane.

perfbot: perfbot: generated NCCL timeline summary: allreduce avg=9.2ms, p99=28.7ms, #calls=4200. serialization spikes at 11:12:43.

matt: that p99 is killer. do we have kernel selection info? maybe quantized kernels are taking different paths when batch shapes change.

anya: attached a small snippet from the nsys event dump (abridged):
```
[GPU0] kernel: matmul_q4   start 0.123s   end 0.128s  duration 5ms
[GPU1] kernel: matmul_q4   start 0.124s   end 0.129s  duration 5ms
[GPU2] kernel: matmul_q8   start 0.125s   end 0.137s  duration 12ms  <-- different kernel selected
[GPU3] kernel: matmul_q4   start 0.126s   end 0.131s  duration 5ms
```
That shows kernel selection diverging between ranks (q4 vs q8), probably due to dynamic path in kernel selector.

carl: yep. kernel heterogeneity + NCCL reduction means slower rank drags others. also noticed KV cache eviction bursts aligned with allreduce windows — we may be hitting retire/refresh logic too often.

zara: is it possible the larger batches change sequence packing so some ranks get heavier sequences and others have many short ones? our continuous batching picks by time window then packs by token count, so edge cases exist.

matt: proposed short-term mitigations:
- reduce opt_batcher.window_ms back to 20
- enable rank-aware packing (prefer balancing token counts across replicas) behind a flag
- force uniform kernel selection by overriding selector for suspect models (diagnostic only)

anya: ran a quick experiment with forced selector (fallback=q4) across ranks, replayed a sample. p99 allreduce dropped to 12ms and overall throughput regained ~6%.

infra-bot: deploy job 2026-06-04T18:05:21Z started: canary config = batching.window_ms=20, selector.force_q4=true (flag: runtime.force_kernel=q4).

carl: nice! that suggests selector divergence is the main root cause. but we should still address KV retire churn — it amplifies the stalls when ranks are misbalanced.

zara: i'll instrument the KV retire path to add a per-rank retire histogram and push a small perf run. can someone give me the perfetto filter chain they used?

anya: used filter:
- group by process/gpu
- show cudaMemcpyAsync / kernel_launch / ncclAllReduce / nvtx annotations
- color by duration > 5ms
Also exported CSV for kernel durations.

matt: long-term: kernel selector should consider global replica shapes (cheap summary: max/min tokens per rank) before picking per-rank kernel. and batching heuristic should optionally do rank-aware packing when in multi-GPU mode. we can add a fast approximate balancer with O(1) per-request overhead.

perfbot: perf regression alert: job 2026-06-03 04:22:10 showed +14% p99 token latency vs baseline after batching heuristic change. ticket created: PERF-7843.

anya: next steps I propose:
1) roll-canary revert batching.window_ms -> 20 (inflight)
2) temp force kernel q4 on problematic model(s) for 24h and monitor perfetto/NCCL metrics
3) add KV retire histograms + perf job to reproduce with synthetic skewed lengths
4) spec for selector-global-shape feature (matt/zara)

carl: agree. i'll pair with zara on the KV histograms. anya can you paste the perfetto link for the forced-selector run?

anya: perfetto link (forced selector run): https://perfetto.dev/trace/FAKE_TRACE_ID_Q4_FORCED — looks much cleaner, all ranks aligned.

matt: i'll start a simple PR to add rank-summary to the selector and an opt-in balancer. will tag you all.

zara: thanks — i'll schedule the perf run and drop results in this thread. :thumbsup:

anya: thanks team. good repro and a clear mitigation path.

perfbot: note: attach logs at /var/artifacts/perf/PERF-7843/ (automated).
